snip.t: Children with marasmus are often low weight-for-height and have a reduced mid-upper arm circumference, as well as a head that appears large relative to the rest of their body.

Measures of normal growth include:
- height/length
- weight
- head circumference
-Mid upper arm circumference.
• Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) should be used for nutritional\nassessment for children > 6months of age.

snip.t: • Mid upper arm circumference (MUAC) less than 11 cm min in a child 1–5 years old)\n(for children between the ages of 1 and 5 years). • Wheezy breathing\n• Hypothermia (body temperature < 35.5°C)

Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC): Measured using specialized tape with color indicators (red: severely malnourished, yellow: moderately malnourished, green: normal); used for children and pregnant women.
